recent_posts.title: Mastering Storytelling Techniques for Design Presentations
recent_posts.summary: Crafting captivating narratives in design involves a three-pillared framework: Plotlines, Poetry, and Pixels. This framework helps designers articulate their thoughts clearly and engagingly. It starts with composing a structured plotline tailored to various audiences and purposes. Infusing the story with personal perspectives and creative passions adds depth and relatability. Finally, weaving in visual elements - 'pixels' - enhances engagement, clarity, and retention, making the presentation memorable and impactful.

recent_posts.title: Behind the design: Adobe’s new splash screens
recent_posts.summary: Adobe has redesigned the splash screens for its Creative Cloud and Substance 3D desktop apps, featuring vibrant commissioned artwork that celebrates the creative community. The updated designs emphasize the artist's work and integrate feedback from product teams to ensure a seamless user experience. Key changes include larger artwork, placing the artist's name prominently, and incorporating elements from Adobe's design system, Spectrum 2. The redesign highlights Adobe's brand while fostering creativity and community.

recent_posts.title: Ask Adobe Design: What are the non-design skills you rely on in your work?
recent_posts.summary: Five Adobe designers share key non-design skills that have shaped their careers, such as curiosity, business acumen, playfulness, system mapping, and the art of listening. These skills help designers push boundaries, better understand user needs, drive strategy, tackle complex problems, and enhance team collaboration.

recent_posts.title: Research basics every designer should know
recent_posts.summary: Understanding research fundamentals is crucial for designing better products. Methods include qualitative and quantitative research, each providing unique insights into user behavior. The article stresses the importance of asking the right questions, selecting appropriate methodologies, and effectively presenting findings. Creativity in research processes and caring about the results are key to making impactful products.

recent_posts.title: Advice for making the most of an indirect career path to design
recent_posts.summary: Switching to a design career from a less direct path can bring unique advantages and fulfillment. Combining past experiences with new skills can create a unique approach to design. Learning essential tools, staying open to feedback, practicing frequently, and leveraging hobbies and education are key to success. Embrace opportunities, rethink application of current skills, and counter imposter syndrome to thrive in the design industry.

recent_posts.title: Designing design systems: Supporting implementation and adoption
recent_posts.summary: Design systems need thoughtful guidance and constant support to be effective. Spectrum, Adobe's design system, serves a large team and requires meticulous documentation, ongoing updates, and active collaboration. To ensure proper usage, it's essential to create an infrastructure for documentation, maintain communication channels for updates, and facilitate feedback and support. By sharing knowledge and fostering collaboration, a design system can achieve consistency and coherence across various products.

recent_posts.title: What does an EA for a design executive do?
recent_posts.summary: Robert Martin, an Executive Assistant at Adobe, supports three senior design executives by managing their schedules, prioritizing their meetings, and anticipating their needs. He emphasizes the importance of relationship building and communication, utilizing tools like Outlook and Slack to stay informed and connected. Martin also highlights his involvement with community initiatives and his passion for supporting creative teams and fostering diversity within Adobe.

recent_posts.title: Four principles for successful cross-team collaboration
recent_posts.summary: Effective cross-team collaboration involves establishing credibility, building trust, making space for others to contribute, and reinforcing the humanity of colleagues. These principles help manage the 'white space' between diverse teams, ensuring cohesive and creative solutions while minimizing bureaucratic obstacles. By doing so, teams can better serve their customers and drive innovation.

recent_posts.title: Ask Adobe Design: How can applicants stand out when interviewing for design jobs?
recent_posts.summary: Design hiring managers from Adobe share advice on standing out in design job interviews. They emphasize the importance of highlighting collaborative problem-solving skills, demonstrating humility, and understanding the company and team's context. Effective storytelling, showing the impact of your work, and displaying genuine enthusiasm are key to making a strong impression. Additionally, preparing for potential challenges and being able to discuss your learning experiences and professional growth can set you apart as a candidate.

recent_posts.title: Should you pursue a career in design engineering?
recent_posts.summary: Design engineering is an interdisciplinary field combining design and engineering skills to create and improve user experiences. Design engineers engage in activities such as high-fidelity prototyping, building design systems, and refining user interfaces with a keen attention to detail. The role is versatile and responds to the growing need for collaboration between designers and developers. Interested individuals can get started by prototyping, contributing to design systems, or undertaking small UI engineering projects. The future looks promising for hybrid designer-engineer professionals, aided by advancements in design tools and AI.

top_posts.title: Don’t design for your users
top_posts.summary: Designing for a current user without considering the long-term goals of the product adds chaos to the design process. To ensure alignment, designers should focus on challenge people who represent different categories and drive product development.

top_posts.title: Six human skills that will future-proof your design career
top_posts.summary: As AI advances rapidly, designers need to adapt by leveraging distinctly human skills. Beyond technical abilities, designers should focus on core competencies like taste, systems thinking, vision, connection building, empathy, storytelling, and unique personal qualities. By embracing adaptability and emphasizing human-centric attributes, designers can ensure their relevance and thrive in an increasingly automated landscape.
